citation: Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, Government Medical College Srinagar. Antibiogram of blood, urine, and pus and body fluids, July 2023 to December 2023. Srinagar: Government Medical College; 2024.
reporting: Percent susceptible, all locations together. Blood: Gram-positive (MRSA, MSSA, MR-CoNS, MS-CoNS, Enterococcus) and Gram-negative tables giving each organism's share of isolates but no isolate numbers (organism counts on page 1). Urine: Gram-negative and Gram-positive tables with the number of isolates. Pus and body fluids: one list of percentages per organism (organism counts on page 7, no n in the lists).
method: Not stated. The report says vancomycin was not tested for staphylococci (MIC method required), colistin and polymyxins are not reported (MIC only), "-" means intrinsically resistant or not tested, and patterns for fewer than 30 isolates are not given (CLSI), although blood E. coli (20 isolates) and Klebsiella (16) are shown.

verification.note: Scanned PDF, read from page images (scanned PDF). Two separate readings of every table: pass 1 from whole pages rendered at scale 2.5 (pages 1 to 3 from crops at scale 3 to 3.5), pass 2 from crops at scale 3 to 5 (tables cut into left and right halves, column headers read from rotated crops). The two readings were compared by script: 278 of 278 values and counts agreed; no cell was unreadable.

notes: Half-yearly antibiogram (July to December 2023) of the Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, GMC Srinagar, with sections for blood, urine, and pus and body fluids; no location split, so every row is all settings. The blood tables print each organism's share of isolates (e.g. E. coli 7.8% of 255 Gram-negative isolates) but no isolate numbers, and the pus lists print none, so those rows have no n; the organism counts of pages 1 (blood), 4 (urine) and 7 (pus) are recorded as counts. MRSA were 42% and MSSA 58% of blood S. aureus, MR-CoNS 63% and MS-CoNS 37% of blood CoNS. Urine MRSA (4 isolates) and MSSA (6) percentages such as 65% and 93% cannot be produced by 4 or 6 isolates (source error, recorded as printed). Several pus figures repeat the January to June 2023 report exactly (e.g. E. coli tigecycline 97, amikacin 75, cefoperazone-sulbactam 68, piperacillin-tazobactam 58, ceftriaxone 22, ampicillin-sulbactam 7; MRSA tetracycline 86, erythromycin 27; Enterococcus vancomycin 88, high-level gentamicin 55), while others differ. Pus lists include "Ceftazidime-tazobactam" and the urine table "Ceftazidime + Clavulanic acid", which have no drug key and are not recorded. Candida susceptibility was not done (no reagents).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 154 cells (including the seeded 40% sample of 62), all 22 row n values and all 30 counts were read blind from the page images (scale 3 to 5, tables cropped) and compared with the file by script: 0 differences, nothing corrected.

Stratum checks: the report has no location split, so set "all" is right for every row; specimens blood, urine, and pus and body fluids (recorded as pus) confirmed; organisms and MRSA/MSSA, MR-CoNS/MS-CoNS rows confirmed. Blood and pus rows print no isolate numbers (n null is right); urine rows print n (400, 150, 170, 190, 4, 6).

Cells not kept, re-read at scale 5 on page 6: urine Enterococcus amikacin 45 and gentamicin 50 (intrinsic), urine MRSA (n=4) amikacin 65, levofloxacin 21, ciprofloxacin 15, fosfomycin 93, gentamicin 57 and MSSA (n=6) amikacin 70, fosfomycin 95 (cautions) are all printed that way (source, not transcription).

Figures repeated from the January to June 2023 report, confirmed on both reports' pages as printed: pus E. coli tigecycline 97, amikacin 75, cefoperazone-sulbactam 68, piperacillin-tazobactam 58, ceftriaxone 22, ampicillin-sulbactam 7 (6 of 8 shared figures); Klebsiella tigecycline 94, cefoperazone-sulbactam 54; Pseudomonas piperacillin-tazobactam 72 (and ceftazidime-tazobactam 57, not recorded); MRSA linezolid 100, tetracycline 86, erythromycin 27; MSSA linezolid 100, tetracycline 90, erythromycin 64; Enterococcus linezolid 100, vancomycin 88, high-level gentamicin 55.

The build copy check (copyChecks: 6 identical figures that are at least 80% of the shared ones) flags none of these rows when run over the GMC Srinagar files (E. coli is 6 of 8, 75%), so a sentence on the repeat was added to the pus E. coli row note.
